surfaces.part: notice board panel with paper sheets (vertical face)

answer.evidence: This is a framed notice board on two posts, not a column. The only top-like feature is a 1-row highlight at row 3 on the header beam. Rows 4-6 below it are a flat brown front-facing strip with no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so the beam reads as a vertical face. The width profile widens at rows 4-6 (31-32 px) and then settles at 28 px for rows 8-22, with no ellipse. The board face (rows 8-22) carries white and cream paper sheets and is flat. Rows 23-31 are two narrow posts (8 px total) with a gap between them. Nothing shows a horizontal top surface, so it is front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden notice board with torn paper scraps, and it reads clearly. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels), which matches Beodeul practice. The shading is shallow: only 8 distinct colours in the whole piece, against 11-40 in the references. The wood has about 3 steps (dark frame, mid board, a light edge) where the stall and well use 5-6 per material. The paper is just white plus one grey. At 7 visible tones per tile it falls below the hedge (9) and well below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 10%, close to the stall's 13%, so the board face is mostly flat with little plank grain or per-clump variation. Next to the references it looks thinner and flatter, so it fails.

surfaces.part: notice board face with posts and pinned papers

answer.evidence: This is a notice board: a wooden frame with two side posts and a board face holding paper notices. It is not a column. The top header (rows 3-6, width 22-32) is a front-facing brown strip. Its only lower boundary is the dark outline at row 7, which is the same line that borders the rest of the frame. There is no lighter or darker front-edge line and no eave shadow, so it reads as a beam or cornice, not a horizontal surface. The widths are 20, 22, 31, 32, 32, 30, then 28 for rows 8-22. The header is only slightly wider than the body, so it is not an elliptical cap plate. Below it the board face (rows 8-22, about 15 rows) is a vertical face with the posts running down to row 31. The result is a front elevation with no real top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden notice board with pinned paper notes. Its outline is a dark brown, tinted to match the wood (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels), so it avoids the black-sticker look. It uses only 8 colours in total, and the wood ramp has about 3 steps (frame, board, dark edge). The paper scraps have about 2 steps. The Beodeul pieces of similar complexity carry about 5-6 steps per material: the well has 20 visible tones per tile, the stall has 17 and the hedge has 9, against 7 for the candidate. Near-flat coverage is 10%, close to the stall's 13%, but the board face and frame read as fairly smooth with little grain, knots or per-plank highlights. The papers are plain light blocks with little detail. Next to the references it looks thinner and flatter in shading depth, even though it is cleanly drawn and the outline is acceptable. A careful artist would want more wood grain and a deeper ramp on the frame and papers.

answer.evidence: This is a notice board: a flat front-facing frame with a header beam (rows 3-6), a board face (rows 8-21) and two thin posts (rows 23-30, width 8 in total, so about 4 px each). The width profile steps from 20 to 32 at the top beam and then stays flat at 28. It never widens and then narrows again, so there is no ellipse. The beam is one front-facing strip: row 3 is a lighter highlight, rows 4-6 are a uniform brown, and row 7 is only the dark outline. There is no front-edge line with eave shadow below it, and no horizontal surface is visible anywhere. The cap does not overhang a shaft as a rounded plate, so this reads as a flat front elevation. It is not a column-like object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wooden notice board with a few paper scraps. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown and counts as a dark wood tone rather than black. It has 7 visible tones per tile, which is below the stall (17) and well (20) and a little below the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 10%, close to the stall's 13%, so there are some flat fills. The brown wood frame and board show only about 3 lightness steps, with little grain or per-plank shading, whereas the references carry 5-6 steps with grain and clustered texture. The paper scraps are mostly flat light blocks with little detail. It looks flatter and thinner than the stall and well it should sit beside, so I fail it.

surfaces.part: notice board panel with paper scraps

answer.evidence: This is a framed notice board seen face-on, not a column. The header at rows 2-6 is a flat brown strip that widens from 20 to 32 px. It has a dark outline row at row 7, but no lighter or darker front-edge line and no eave shadow, so it is a front-facing beam and not a top surface. The board face at rows 8-22 holds white paper scraps, which are vertical details. The two side posts run down to row 30. Nothing shows an ellipse, a roof plane or contents. The width profile (32, then 28, then 8) gives no ellipse cap. No horizontal surface is visible, so the drawing is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The notice board is a brown wood frame with pale paper scraps, and it uses only 8 distinct colours in total. Each tile shows 7 visible tones, against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. The wood ramp is about 3 steps (light edge, mid, dark), where the references use 5-6 on wood and roof. The board face and the posts have little grain, with only a few paper dots, and 10% of the piece is near-flat 5x5 blocks. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral edge pixels), so it is not a sticker line. Even so, the candidate has less shading depth, less wood grain and fewer paper details than the stall and well beside it, so it looks flatter than the references.
